text:
Washington fired 36 shots on goal to Seattle's 27 and still lost by two, but the numbers say the Capitals were not robbed so much as out-chanced. SEA finished with 5.03 expected goals to WSH's 3.35, and in a simulated replay of every shot Seattle wins 60 percent of the time. The Kraken's edge grew as the game went on: 1.43 to 1.05 in the first period, 1.13 to 0.64 in the second, and 2.48 to 1.65 in the third.

The first period was a swap of goals that ended level at 2-2. Kaapo Kakko opened the scoring for SEA at 6:06, Jordan Kyrou and Alex Ovechkin put WSH ahead, and Jordan Eberle tied it with 11 seconds left in the period on an 8 percent chance. Frederick Gaudreau put SEA in front at 13:24 of the second with a backhand. Boone Jenner tied it for WSH 46 seconds into the third, one of his five shots on goal, and he later had a 34 percent look stopped by Joey Daccord.

The game turned over the last six minutes. Jared McCann restored the lead at 14:33 with a snap shot, and Ryan Winterton finished an 85 percent chance at 17:20 to make it 5-3. Logan Thompson allowed 1.1 goals more than the 27 shots he faced deserved, while Daccord stopped 33 of 36 and finished 0.35 goals better than expected. WSH outhit SEA 31 to 13, but SEA had seven takeaways to one, and every goal in the game came at even strength.
